chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was first appointed [to prophethood], he would fast continuously until it was said: 'He will not break his fast.' And he would break his fast for days until it was said: 'He will not fast.' Then he abandoned that and fasted one day and skipped one day, which is the fasting of David (peace be upon him). Then he abandoned that, and he passed away while fasting on two Thursdays with a Wednesday in between them.

key_terms.صَوْمُ دَاوُدَ: The fasting of David, referring to fasting one day and skipping the next

ai.seo_question: What was the specific fasting pattern of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) at the time of his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Khisal* outlines the chronological evolution of the Prophet Muhammad’s (SAWW) fasting regimen, moving from initial continuous fasting to the balanced practice of Dawud, and finally to the specific pattern of fasting on two Thursdays and skipping one Wednesday each month. This progression highlights the Sunnah of moderation, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence, and underscores the significance of Thursday as a day of special devotion and preparation for the upcoming week.
